title: Go SDK response models, streaming transformers, and retry strategies
creator: Asha Patel
description:
Problem: The current Go SDK lacks a concise, ergonomic pattern for decoding structured outputs (JSON objects, typed models) when responses arrive as streaming token events. Engineers have implemented ad-hoc decoders in multiple places which leads to duplication, fragile partial-json handling, and inconsistent retry semantics for transient network errors.

Goal: Deliver a set of typed response models + generics-based helper primitives and a streaming transformer helper that: 1) safely accumulates partial frames into typed structs, 2) exposes a small surface for consumers to handle incremental tokens (for UI/CLI streaming), 3) integrates with unified retry/backoff policy and preserves idempotency and resume semantics where applicable.

Scope: 
- Define canonical typed models (response envelope, event types) for generation, chat, and embedding-streaming flows.
- Implement a generics-first Decode[T any] helper that accepts an io.Reader or channel of []byte and yields typed T when the stream contains a full object.
- Provide a StreamingTransformer that emits: token events, structured-event callbacks, and an optional final typed object.
- Wire retry strategy hooks into the stream layer so retries can be attempted before the caller has committed side-effects; expose idempotency guidance for callers.
- Add end-to-end examples and integration tests.

Non-goals: 
- Not changing the public REST API contract of Redwood. 
- Not adding server-side support for resumable partial streams (server feature request).

Trade-offs considered: 
- Buffering until full JSON object vs emitting partial structured data: We will provide configuration flags. Default favors safety (buffer until valid JSON) to avoid passing partial/inconsistent typed objects. Consumers can opt into a streaming-merge mode for token-level UI.
- Generics vs interface-driven APIs: We use Go generics (Go 1.20+) for Parse[T any] helpers to reduce boilerplate; also expose interface-backed decoders for legacy users.
acceptance_criteria: Typed response models defined for generation/chat/embeddings and documented in SDK reference
Decode[T] helper implemented with unit tests covering partial-frame and multi-object streams
StreamingTransformer exposes token-level callbacks and final typed object when available
Retry/backoff integrated and configurable; integration tests simulate transient gRPC/HTTP failures
Examples and migration guide added to docs (CONFLUENCE/Drive link) and examples repo
tasks: Design API surface and review with SDK/PM (done)
Add StreamingTransformer with configured backpressure and cancelation semantics
Add tests: unit, fuzz (partial json), and integration (network flakiness)
Write examples: examples/typed_decode and examples/streaming_chat in go-examples repo
Performance microbenchmarks and regression guard in CI
comments: 2026-03-02 — Asha Patel: Initial design doc uploaded. Decided to default to buffering until complete JSON to avoid partial-struct leaks. See design link.

2026-03-04 — Liam Chen: Spike implemented Decode[T] prototype using bytes.Buffer + json.Decoder with UseNumber to preserve numeric fidelity. Prototype found edge cases with back-to-back JSON objects on a single stream; added loop to decode until EOF of a single frame.

2026-03-06 — Jordan Reyes (review): Concern about allocating large buffers for long-running streams. Suggested configurable maxBufferSize and emitting a tokenized fallback. Added task to add backpressure signals to transformer.
2026-03-08 — Liam Chen: Updated prototype to use a reusable buf pool to reduce GC pressure. Benchmarked with 10k small messages: allocations reduced ~40%. Added bench results to PR 361.

2026-03-09 — Security review note: No sensitive material is parsed by these helpers; however, we must ensure KMS keys are not logged in retries. Marked security_review_required=false but added checklist to avoid sensitive logging.

2026-03-10 — PR feedback from SDK team: API naming suggestions — Rename ParseTo[T] -> Decode[T] for clarity. Add context.Context param to all streaming entry points for cancellation. Updated code accordingly in branch feature/stream-decode.

2026-03-11 — Integration test failure: Simulated 502 during streaming resulted in partial typed object being returned and caller applying side-effects. Fix: roll back default to not return typed object until stream EOF or explicit final event. Added integration test for this case.

2026-03-12 — UX request (PM Nora Li): Add a small example that shows how to render streaming tokens to a terminal while still producing a final typed object. Implemented StreamingTransformer.StreamTo chan string + Final() T pattern. Needs API review.
2026-03-13 — Liam Chen: Preparing PR 361 for review. Remaining items: expand README examples, add fuzzer for partial JSON sequences, and update CHANGELOG. Target merge window: 2026-03-20.
